angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 419,507 km at 188.62 pc = 0.03 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.3016 +/- 0.0152 mas (same row, RUWE 1.48): 188.62 pc, no zero-point correction; the RUWE is high, so the astrometry fits a single star poorly, and the parallax is used as published
radiusSource: Radius 0.603 +/- 0.06 solar radii from Q1-Q17 DR25 KOI Table, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of Kepler-1939 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/Kepler_KOI_docs.html): 419,507 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.648 +/- 0.056 solar masses from Q1-Q17 DR25 KOI Table, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of Kepler-1939 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/Kepler_KOI_docs.html); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4353 +/- 118 K from Q1-Q17 DR25 KOI Table, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Kepler-1939 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/Kepler_KOI_docs.html). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Q1-Q17 DR25 KOI Table, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Kepler-1939 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/Kepler_KOI_docs.html)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/kepler-1939.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.689, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
